interactionPartnersRead: Uniswap V2 pair semantics (swap/_update, sync, skim, _mintFee)
summary: No new High/Medium/Low. The story-051 fixes add no new value-extraction path. Four informational items: two correct premises in the fix's NatSpec and in the code-scan output (who receives a donation; whether the V2 fee switch is on), one confirms that quote poisoning through balanceOf is weaker than the swap-based L-22/L-23 class, and one records the economic effect of the hook-guard window. Q-21 reproduces exactly at $636. The fix leaves the threshold unchanged and makes it computable from quotePool.

findings.description: The NatSpec (and code-scan L-25 valueShiftAnalysis) frames the fix as moving an unsynced donation from 'absorbed into our swap and LP mint' to 'accrues pro rata to LPs'. Pre-fix, the donation already accrued pro rata to LPs: the router fixes amountOut from stored reserves for input s, UniswapV2Pair.swap credits balance-(reserve-out)=s+D as input, and _update sets reserves to balances, folding D into reserves for every LP. The pooler never captured the donation in its output or its LP mint (the mint sees the post-swap synced reserves). What the pre-fix code got wrong was only the balance between the two legs: the pooler's own bought phUSD (or its own sUSDS) was left unpaired on the pooler, where rescueERC20 could still recover it. That is protocol inventory, not donated value. sync() changes when the donation is folded in, from swap time to sizing time. It does not change who receives it.
findings.economicImpact: None. A donation is a gift to LP holders before and after the fix. Its beneficiary is the LP-share split. Per plan §Stage 2 step 4 and decision 5 (BalancerWinddownPlan.md:375, :472), the seed addLiquidity mints to UniPoolerV2, so POL is custodied on the pooler, not an EOA. The pooler is about 100% of LP, minus MINIMUM_LIQUIDITY and feeTo shares, unless EOA 0xc65f…e8db (37.1% of the old BPT) later adds to the V2 pair, in which case it captures its pro-rata share. The Q-21 EOA question affects depth, not POL custody. Simulation (100k/100k, 0.5% sUSDS donation, 100k zap): pre-fix left about 103 phUSD unpaired on the pooler, post-fix leaves dust, and the donation sits in reserves in both cases.
findings.attackScenario: Donate -> wait for keeper pool() -> remove liquidity: the attacker recovers only g*D, where g is its LP share, and loses (1-g)*D. Only authorized poolers can call pool(), so the attacker cannot trigger it. On price impact, a sUSDS donation moves the spot by about D/rS with nothing coming back, while a swap front-run of the same size gets phUSD back and loses only the 0.3% fee. The donation is strictly dominated by the L-22 swap front-run.
findings.profitability: Never profitable. The donor loses (1-g)*D. With g ≤ 37.1% (the EOA's maximum plausible share), at least 62.9% of every donation is lost.
findings.relatedLedger: L-25 8ec2be7d (fix-pending, code-scan FIX-COMPLETE; this does not challenge the verdict). L-22 a846cc40 (wont-fix), not re-filed because this mechanism is weaker, not stronger. CODE-21-003 (same NatSpec line, about the 'overwhelmingly POL' premise). This entry supplies the custody answer CODE-21-003 asked for (plan: LP to UniPoolerV2) and corrects the 'absorbed into our swap' half.
findings.recommendation: Reword the NatSpec at :57-61: an unsynced donation is folded into reserves by swap()'s _update either way, and sync() just makes the reserve-derived s match what swap() credits, so both legs balance. Phase-2 Stage 2 verification (plan :390) should assert pair.balanceOf(UniPoolerV2) == pair.totalSupply() - 1000 - pair.balanceOf(feeTo).

findings.description: Code-scan MR-004 cleared the feeTo interaction with sync() on the premise 'feeTo is off on the mainnet V2 factory'. That premise is false. `cast call 0x5C69bEe701ef814a2B6a3EDD4B1652CB9cc5aA6f feeTo()` returns 0xf38521f130fcCF29dB1961597bc5d2B60F995f85 today, and BalancerWinddownPlan.md:174 already records it as live (UNIfication, Dec 2025). Consequences: (a) at the zap's addLiquidity, _mintFee mints feeTo about 1/6 of the sqrt(k) growth since kLast. That growth includes any donation folded in by sync() (and, pre-fix, by swap) and the swap fees. (b) quotePool computes expectedLP from the pre-fee totalSupply. The fee-on branch of its NatSpec is therefore the live case, not a hypothetical. Our minted LP count is ≥ the quote, so minLP is still a valid floor in LP units, but each LP unit carries the feeTo dilution.
findings.codeSnippet:
uint256 ts = IUniswapV2Pair(_pair).totalSupply();
expectedLP = Math.min((amtS * ts) / rS2, (amtP * ts) / rP2);
findings.economicImpact: Negligible, and no loss of protocol principal. feeTo takes at most 1/6 of the growth, so LP value never falls below its pre-growth level. Swap-fee growth of about 0.15%·V/R_side per traded volume V gives a feeTo share of about 0.025% of supply per one-side-reserve of volume. A donation D yields about D/(12·rS) of supply to feeTo, all of it donated value. The 0.30% swap fee and therefore phusdOut are unaffected.
findings.affectedParties: LP holders (POL) lose 1/6 of donation and fee growth to Uniswap, which the plan already accepts.
findings.relatedLedger: None. Corrects run-21 code-scan setAside MR-004 (disposition 'cleared' rested on a false fact; the conclusion survives).
findings.recommendation: Update the quotePool NatSpec to say the V2 fee switch is on and expectedLP is therefore a conservative unit floor. Have the setAside record carry the corrected premise so later runs do not inherit 'feeTo is off'.
findings.confidence: high (on-chain read at scan time; feeTo is governance-mutable)

findings.type: quote-poisoning (tolerance-bounded MEV) — not strictly stronger than L-22/L-23
findings.description: quotePool now sizes from balanceOf(pair). Before the fix, an unsynced donation could not move the quote. Now it can. A sUSDS donation that is mined before the keeper reads the quote lowers both phusdOut and expectedLP, because phUSD looks more expensive and reserves look deeper. The keeper's floors are then too lenient. If the attacker reclaims the donation with the permissionless skim() before pool(), the true execution sits above those lenient floors, and the attacker can sandwich up to the widened slack. This is the same class as L-22 / L-23: floors derived from manipulable spot, with tolerance widened by a stale quote. It is not a stronger version of it. A swap at the end of block N-1 poisons the quote through getReserves() just as well, then and now. The swap leaves the attacker holding phUSD and costs about 0.6% round-trip fees plus arbitrage exposure across the block boundary. The donation leaves the whole manipulation amount unsynced and skimmable by anyone (generalized skim bots) for at least one block boundary, so its capital is fully at risk. Inside a single block, a donation before pool() is synced and lost to LPs, which is dominated as shown in ECON-21-001. The fix also removes one griefing lever: before it, a donation between quote and execution stranded tokens or forced an InsufficientLP revert even without any price move. Now it moves the price only by D/rS, exactly like any other reserve change, and is bounded by the same floors.
findings.economicImpact: Bounded by the keeper's tolerance on a quote that may be stale, the same bound as L-22 and L-23, on POL only. No new extraction ceiling.
findings.attackScenario:
1. End of block N-1: donate D sUSDS to the pair with no sync, so the keeper's quotePool reads lowered floors.
2. Top of block N, in the attacker's bundle: skim(D) to recover it, then front-run swap, keeper pool(), back-run.
3. The swap-based variant (step 1 = swap) already achieves this at strictly lower capital risk.
findings.profitability: Less profitable than the swap-based variant because D is exposed to third-party skim across the block boundary. It cannot outperform the existing L-22/L-23 mechanism.
findings.relatedLedger: Not re-filed. L-22 a846cc40 (wont-fix) triageReason: "Owner triage 2026-10-01: intended by design. Owner: \"That's the nature of tolerance. We're literally tolerating an attack of this size.\" ... Disposition does NOT cover ... L-23 (shared-venue floor staleness), whose stale-floor mechanism could widen the effective tolerance beyond t." L-23 c15c71fd (wont-fix) triageReason: "... The frequency of NFT minting is not live trading. This scenario is a lightning strike rather than a common inconvenience. ... Operational guidance retained: do not batch both calls in one block; quote the second after the first is mined." Deliberately poisoning the quote is a distinct trigger from L-23's accidental collision. However, a swap could already deliberately poison the quote before this fix, so the balanceOf read adds no capability. Recall note for triage: L-23's 'lightning strike' rationale covers accidental same-block collisions, not an attacker who poisons the quote on purpose (by either lever). If the owner wants that covered explicitly, it belongs on L-22/L-23, not as a new finding.
findings.recommendation: Operational only. The keeper should check that pair.balanceOf equals getReserves() when it quotes (no pending donation), and should bound its floors against an off-chain reference such as PhusdStableMinter's $1 mint price, not spot alone. No code change.

findings.description: Until setHook, every index-4 NFTMinterV2.mint reverts UniPoolerV2__HookNotSet. The revert is atomic. Payment transferFrom and price growth roll back, and no PSM donation, sUSDS wrap or nudge collection happens, so no price, rate or debt state changes. Knock-on effect: BatchNFTMinter.batchMint (phoenix-nft-staking BatchNFTMinter.sol:238-290) loops nftMinter.mint(dispatcherIndex, …). If its dispatcherIndex is 4, the usual configuration since UniPoolerV2 donates to batchMinter, the whole batch reverts as well. Meanwhile the NudgeStreamer keeps releasing nudge that was already collected into the batchMinter's deliverable pot. Nothing new enters, because donations need mints. The first batchMint after setHook collects the pot that built up during the window. This is the nudge's normal incentive behaviour after any pause or quiet period, and it is capped by nudge already streamed. Compared with the pre-fix behaviour (L-21: mints succeed while accruing zero phUSD mint-debt, an unbacked-mint leak), this is strictly better.
findings.economicImpact: Liveness only, for the cutover window between replaceDispatcher(4) and setHook (plan Stage 2 steps 5→6). No value is lost or mispriced. The accumulated nudge pot goes to the first post-window batch minter, the same as after any quiet period.
findings.attackScenario: None adversarial. The window is owner-controlled.
findings.profitability: n/a. A searcher could race the first post-setHook batchMint for the accumulated pot. That is the nudge's designed incentive, not a leak.
findings.affectedParties: Index-4 minters and batch minters, who are delayed during the window.
findings.relatedLedger: L-21 6867d791 (FIX-COMPLETE per code-scan). Run-21 code-scan setAside MR-002 already covers the ordering.
findings.recommendation: Run replaceDispatcher(4), hook.setDispatcher(UniPoolerV2) and UniPoolerV2.setHook(hook) in one multisig batch so the window is zero blocks.
findings.confidence: medium (BatchNFTMinter.dispatcherIndex == 4 is on-chain config, not verified here)

q21Requantification.verdict: NOT-ADDRESSED (agrees with code-scan); threshold unchanged by the sync fix
q21Requantification.inputs: Seed 19,130 sUSDS ($21.26k, sUSDS ≈ $1.1113) / 21,896 phUSD; phUSD spot $0.97095; exact V2 0.30% zap model (same closed form as _swapAmount).
q21Requantification.effectOfSync: With no pending donation, sync() is a no-op and the threshold is $636. With an unsynced donation, the threshold moves. sUSDS-side donation of 0.1% / 0.5% / 1% of reserve: $615 / $530 / $423. phUSD-side donation of the same sizes: $658 / $745 / $855. Pre-fix, a sUSDS donation was folded in at swap time and the stale-sized swap added D to the input, so the price moved further than the keeper predicted. Post-fix, quotePool (balances) and pool (synced reserves) agree, so a keeper that derives post-zap spot from quotePool now gets the correct threshold. The fix makes Q-21's recommended mitigation ('chunk so post-zap spot ≤ $1') computable on-chain. It does not change the plan-premise error.
q21Requantification.note: The threshold is a function of live reserves at zap time, not of the seed. After the first zap, an arb or Leg A trade, it must be recomputed. Whether EOA 0xc65f…e8db migrates still decides the depth (it would scale the threshold by about 1.59x).

regressionCheck: No change to ATokenDispatcherV2, hooks, NFTMinterV2 or the donation path's economics. No cross-contract value flow added beyond pair.sync() and factory.getPair(). Story-051 calls the sync fix 'ycn20l24', but ycn20l24 is L-24 (dust pre-seed, wont-fix) and the sync finding is L-25 ycn20l25 / 8ec2be7d. Code-scan already flagged this label drift. Reconcile on fingerprint.

Who receives the seed LP comes from the plan document (phStaging2:108 not yet landed); the code does not enforce it.
